title: `podman config` and `podman run --config` support
body:
### Feature request description

[`docker config`](https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/config/) provides a way to define and inject configuration assets inside containers (via [`docker service` command](https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/service/create/#config)). The syntax and behaviour is analogous to the already supported `docker secrets` (swarm-mode only)/`podman secrets`.

Since `podman kube` already supports `ConfigMaps`, some functional implementation has to exist in podman to deal and pass configuration assets to containers.

By enabling this feature, the following derived use cases could be implemented:
* `podman compose` `config`: since docker-compose file reference also [adds support for these config assets](https://docs.docker.com/reference/compose-file/configs/).
* Quadlet `<service>.config` or `Config=<...>` settings.

The major benefit of this approach is that it allows having self-contained containerized apps (e.g.: in bootc-based/immutable OSes) with explicit and distinctive handling of assets (secrets, config). A big downside of containerized apps (vs. packaged based) outside the kubernetes world is the hassle of distributing and managing config assets, specially in immutable systems.

### Suggest potential solution

* `podman config {create,ls,inspect,exists,rm}` (`exists` is not supported in `docker config`, but it's consistent with `podman secret exists`, which is neither supported by `docker secret`).
* `podman run --config stringArray`: should be analogous to the `podman run --secret` option, and consistent as much as possible with [`docker service create --config`](https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/service/create/#config).

### Have you considered any alternatives?

_No response_

### Additional context

Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here.

comments.body:
I do not think this is a good idea, https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/30140#pullrequestreview-5825795826

> podman compose config: since docker-compose file reference also [adds support for these config assets](https://docs.docker.com/reference/compose-file/configs/).

Configs in docker-compose are implemented client side within the compose command last I looked at it so podman does not need to support this.

> Quadlet <service>.config or Config=<...> settings.

You can just do a regular file bind mount and deploy the config file alongside the quadlet file.
Or use ExecStartPre= to write some one liner creating the config file and then mount that one.
